prose.en: A English in the USA differs considerably from British English. Pronunciation is the most striking difference but there are also a number of differences in vocabulary and spelling as well as slight differences in grammar. Yet, on the whole, speakers of British and American English have little difficulty in understanding each other.

B American spelling is usually simpler. For example, British English words ending in -our and -re, end in -or and -er in American English, e.g. colour/color, centre/center. Words ending -ise in British English end in -ize in US English. There are differences in individual words too, e.g. British 'plough' becomes 'plow'.
C Here are some common US words with their British equivalents.
Note: the fall = autumn    semester = term (academic) [semester is becoming more common in Britain.]
